rules.title: SQL built from a request superglobal
rules.why: Concatenating a superglobal into SQL is direct injection with no mitigating layer.
rules.falsePositiveHints: PDO prepare() + bindParam/execute(array) is safe. Eloquent/query-builder methods parameterize; DB::raw() does not.

rules.title: Request value echoed without escaping
rules.why: Echoing request data unescaped is reflected XSS. Blade's {!! !!} disables escaping that {{ }} would apply.
rules.falsePositiveHints: htmlspecialchars/htmlentities/e() wrapping closes it. Blade {{ }} is escaped and safe.

rules.title: File include or require built from input
rules.why: Local/remote file inclusion leads to source disclosure and, with an uploadable path or a wrapper, remote code execution.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Closed only by an allow-list of permitted filenames. Basename() alone is not sufficient.

rules.title: Dangerous PHP runtime setting
rules.why: display_errors leaks paths, queries and configuration to visitors; allow_url_include turns an LFI into RFI.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Acceptable in a development-only ini. Confirm which file the deployment loads.

rules.title: Go SQL query built with Sprintf or concatenation
rules.why: database/sql supports placeholders; Sprintf into the query defeats them entirely.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Query("... WHERE id = $1", id) is the safe form. Sprintf used only to assemble a static query from constants is Info.

rules.title: Go template escaping bypassed
rules.why: These types tell html/template the content is already safe. text/template performs no contextual escaping at all when rendering HTML.
rules.falsePositiveHints: text/template for non-HTML output (config files, emails, CLI text) is correct and not a finding.

rules.title: Go TLS verification disabled
rules.why: InsecureSkipVerify accepts any certificate, reducing TLS to unauthenticated encryption.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Test files are lower severity, but confirm the flag cannot be reached from a production code path.

rules.title: Rails query built by interpolation
rules.why: ActiveRecord parameterizes hash and array conditions; #{} interpolation inside a SQL string does not.
rules.falsePositiveHints: where("id = ?", id) and where(id: id) are safe. Interpolating a column name from an allow-list is lower severity.

rules.title: Ruby command execution or dynamic evaluation
rules.why: Backticks and system() invoke a shell; send(params[...]) lets a caller invoke arbitrary methods on the object.
rules.falsePositiveHints: system with an argument array avoids the shell. Literal commands are Info.

rules.title: Rails output escaping bypassed
rules.why: html_safe and raw disable ERB's automatic escaping for that value.
rules.falsePositiveHints: html_safe over a developer-authored literal is fine. Over anything derived from params or the database it is a finding.

rules.title: No authentication or authorization filter detected
rules.why: No authentication filters means every controller action is anonymous.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Rack middleware or an upstream gateway may enforce it. Verify.

rules.title: Declared dependencies to inventory for advisory checking
rules.why: Collects the dependency inventory for the Step 4 advisory check.
rules.falsePositiveHints: Not a finding on its own.
